name: Broadsheet
oneLiner: Nonprofit Megaphone as the publication of record on the Google Ad Grant: cool newsprint, black ink and one deep blue, with every claim set like a ledger entry (dated, sourced, forwardable to a board) under a masthead that was printed this morning.
concept:
The buyer is a tired executive director or communications lead who screens vendors for transparency and has to defend a flat monthly fee as overhead to a board. Every competitor answers that person with saturated blue, a logo carousel and a #1 claim. Broadsheet answers with the visual grammar of a respected daily: an ear strip with a real dateline and an edition marker, a masthead under an Oxford rule, a seven-and-five column split with a hairline between, small-caps section labels, tabular numerals, dated figures and sourced footnotes. Numbers are printed the way a paper of record prints them, not the way a SaaS stat card shouts them. The emotional register is calm authority: relief, not excitement.

The ground is cool newsprint, not cream. The page is #FAFAF8, the ledger card is pure white, the ink is #111 and the rules are cool gray. The only chromatic colour anywhere is the brand's deep blue #0A23A2, used as a newspaper uses its one spot colour: the CTA, links, the single italic emphasis in the headline, the 'On the record' ledger header, the Google 5% floor line, the CEO's signature and a duotone portrait plate. There is no red, coral, vermilion, ochre or yellow on the site. That single discipline is what separates it from Amplitude (warm paper, vermilion) and Signed Sentence (oat, forest, ochre), and it makes the rebrand read to 780 existing clients as a sharpening of the blue they already know rather than a rupture.

It fits Nonprofit Megaphone because the company's real assets are documentary, not decorative: 54 case studies, a 5,000-word ungated Ad Grants guide, 618 blog posts, a 60-person named team, an endorsement from Google's first Head of Ad Grants, an inaugural-cohort certification held by nine agencies worldwide, and $48M of managed media. That is a publisher's inventory. The site treats it as one: a ledger with as-of dates, a CTR chart with Google's deactivation floor drawn in, a typographic client roll that reads as a subscriber list, and a human row where Google's endorsement sits on one side of a hairline and Amber Snow's signed guarantee sits on the other. Nothing is a costume: the dateline is the real CMS 'last reviewed' date, the edition marker is the real 'figures updated' month, and the certification line in the ear is a fact.
distinctFrom: It is the only direction printed in black ink and a single blue on cool white newsprint, structured like a daily paper (ear strip, masthead under an Oxford rule, column rules, small-caps labels, a ledger), where the others are warm-toned, multi-accent or blue-dominant.

palette.note: Cool newsprint white, the page ground everywhere. Deliberately not cream: no warmth in the paper, so the direction cannot be mistaken for Amplitude or Signed Sentence.
Pure white for the ledger card, tables, report plates and form fields, separated from the ground by a 1px rule, never by shadow.
Black ink for headlines, body, chart series, the Oxford rule and the thick rules above major sections. 17.5:1 on newsprint.
Cool gray for captions, labels, footnotes and sub copy. 7.0:1 on #FAFAF8 and 7.4:1 on white, so it passes AA at 11px labels and AAA at body size.
Cool hairline gray for column rules, table borders, the ear strip rule and card frames. The site's main structural device.
Chart tracks, zebra rows, disabled states.

The brand's deep blue and the only chromatic colour on the site. The CTA (nav and hero identical), links and their underlines, the one italic phrase in the headline, the ledger header block, the dashed Google 5% floor line, the pull-quote glyph, the CEO's signature and the duotone portrait plate. 11.3:1 on newsprint, 11.9:1 with white text on it. Hover darkens to #071A7C.
Hover and active state for the blue button and links. Never used as a fill on its own.
Lightest blue for the duotone plate ground, selected table rows and the eligibility checker's progress track. Ink on it is 16:1.

typography.display: Newsreader (Google Fonts), variable opsz 6..72, weights 400 and 500, italic 400 for the one emphasis phrase per headline. opsz 72 for h1 and h2, opsz 36 for ledger figures, opsz 18 for pull quotes and the signed note. Small caps (font-variant-caps: all-small-caps) for section labels: 'The Google Ad Grant', 'On the record', 'Account CTR'.
typography.body: Schibsted Grotesk (Google Fonts) 400/500/600 for body, deck, nav, buttons, table text and all metadata labels (11.5px uppercase, +0.08em, weight 500). No substitution needed; both families are on Google Fonts.
typography.mono: None on the marketing surface. Tabular figures come from font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums in both families. Geist Mono (Google Fonts) is reserved for the client-reports product and account IDs inside redacted report plates, where it marks 'this is data, not copy'.
typography.scaleNotes: h1 72px / 0.98 / -0.025em, Newsreader 400, opsz 72, with one italic phrase in blue as the emphasis device (never bold spans); 44px / 1.0 on phones. h2 52px / 1.02 / -0.02em. h3 28px / 1.15. Deck (hero sub) 17px / 1.5 Schibsted in ink, max 596px; body 17px / 1.5, max 68ch; small body 13.5px in #56565A for fine print only, never the only place a required fact appears. Pull quote and signed note 18px Newsreader italic / 1.28. Ledger figures 34px Newsreader with tabular-nums and a 15px superscript '+' in secondary ink; 32px on phones. Labels 11.5px Schibsted 500 uppercase +0.08em (11px on phones, the floor). Small-caps labels 16px Newsreader 500 +0.08em. Chart: labels 13px Schibsted, values 15px Newsreader 500, ticks 11px; the SVG viewBox is drawn at the chart's rendered width (406px) so SVG text is never scaled below the 11px floor. Buttons 15px/600 Schibsted, 16.5px vertical padding (48px tall), 2px radius, with an optional 11.5px uppercase tag ('15 min') separated by a hairline; nav button 14px/600. The only radii on the site are 2px (buttons, inputs) and 0 (everything else). Rules: 1px hairline #D9D9D6 between sections, 1px ink above major sections, and the 2px-over-1px Oxford rule under the masthead only.

layout:
- Grid and rhythm: 12 columns, 1200px container, 24px gutters, 48px side margins (16px on phone), 8px base spacing. Vertical rhythm is set by rules, not card padding: a 1px cool hairline between every section, a 1px ink rule above major ones, the Oxford rule (2px over 1px) under the masthead. Sections are editorial pairs (7/5 or 5/7 with a vertical hairline) rather than centred stacks; cards exist only as white plates with a hairline frame. Accessibility contract shared with the other directions: 48px minimum targets, 3px #0A23A2 focus ring, 17px body, AA at every size, CSS-only reveals.
- 0. Ear strip (32px, hairline beneath). Left: the dateline, driven by the CMS 'last reviewed' date ('Tuesday, September 22, 2026'). Centre: the factual masthead line ('Est. 2016 · One of nine inaugural Google-certified agencies · 60+ people'). Right: a blue square and 'Figures updated Sep 2026' from the CMS last-updated field, then 'Client reports →' in blue (the login that signals a real product behind the sales page). No volume or issue number, ever. Phone: dateline and edition marker only.
- 1. Masthead (70px, Oxford rule beneath). Vector megaphone mark in blue and ink; wordmark 'Nonprofit Megaphone' in Newsreader 27px with 'Megaphone' italic. Links: Ad Grant, Services, Case studies, Guides, Team, Pricing; the active link is blue with a 2px blue underline. Right: the blue 'Book a free call' button, identical in colour to the hero button so the action colour is learned once.
- 2. Hero (7/5, one column rule between, 1px ink rule beneath). Lead column: small-caps kicker 'The Google Ad Grant' in blue beside the label '$10,000 a month in search ads for every eligible nonprofit'; h1 'Ten thousand dollars a month, properly spent.' with 'properly spent.' as the italic blue phrase; 17px deck; action row = blue 'Book a free call · 15 min' beside the ghost 'See a real account report · PDF · redacted'; the exits line 'Am I eligible? 4 questions · no email' (blue, underlined) with 'Flat monthly fee · No % of ad spend' after a hairline; the guarantee line 'Unhappy with the work? Meet our CEO and we pay you $25.' The foot of the column splits into two ruled cells so the hero reads as three columns across the bottom: left, the Michelle Hurtado endorsement with a blue quote glyph and 'Google's first Global Head of Ad Grants' in blue; right, the signed note: a blue duotone portrait plate, 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy.', Amber Snow's signature drawn in blue, and 'Email Amber directly' as a plain-text blue link. Ledger column: a white card with a hairline frame. Header is the page's one block of #0A23A2 ('On the record', the Google Partner badge, 'As of Sep 2026') with the megaphone's signal arcs drawn in white at low opacity; four ruled rows (780+, $48M+, 100%, 1 of 9) in tabular Newsreader; an inline SVG CTR chart (three published case studies as ink bars, Google's 5% floor as a dashed blue line at a computed x, ticks at 0/10/20/30%, the 'unmanaged median' bar hatched and labelled ILLUSTRATIVE in the chart itself); a footnote naming the two-consecutive-month deactivation rule and the source.
- 3. Trust strip (70px, ink rule above, hairline below). Left cell '780+ clients on record / 54 published case studies · updated monthly'. Right: six client marks capped at six so nothing compresses, set as a typographic roll (serif small caps, italic serif, tracked grotesk) with one slot reserved for a licensed monochrome logo (Scouting America) to prove the two coexist. Static, no carousel.
- 4. '01 The rules' (full width, then 7/5). A three-column policy table in the register of a public notice: Requirement / What Google does if you miss it / What we do about it, one row each for the $10,000 monthly cap, the 5% CTR floor and two-month deactivation, mandatory conversion tracking, the 1% and 2% keyword quality rules, the annual programme survey. Beneath it on the right, the eligibility checker: four questions with a blue progress rule, honest end states for hospitals, schools and government entities, no email required; the end card offers the call.
- 5. '02 The account, every month' (5/7). Left: the one-sentence monthly note as a white plate: named account lead, duotone portrait, client name and month in the header, the real sentence about what changed, dated and signed, rotating from the CMS. Right: a real monthly report rendered as a statement: utilisation vs the $10,000 cap drawn as a thin rule meter, CTR vs the dashed blue 5% floor, compliance checks 14/14, conversions, and a 'named account lead replies within 1 business day' tag. Screenshots carry a visible REDACTED label, never a blur. A 'Forward to board' PDF action sits on the statement.
- 6. '03 Case studies' (4/4/4). Three long-form studies with a fixed KPI trio in the header (CTR, conversion rate, outcome per month) so all 54 read comparably, before/after in tabular figures, a named and titled quote, and a link to the full filterable table (Organization, Vertical, Input, Outcome, Period; sortable) with the 12 vertical filters.
- 7. '04 What it costs' (7/5). A price-range table for Ad Grant management (flat monthly fee, no percent of spend, what is included, typical onboarding time), the 100% acquisition guarantee stated as a clause, and the $25 meet-the-CEO promise typeset as fine print with Amber Snow's signature line and her plain-text email. This section is the nav's 'Pricing' anchor.
- 8. '05 Other services' (full width). A hairline-ruled seven-row index (Ad Grant, Content, SEO, VisitorEmail, Remarketing, Microsoft Ads, Spanish Ad Creation), each with a one-line description, a number, and a 'from' price where leadership will publish one. No icons.
- 9. '06 The people on your account' (full width). Natural-colour team photography with a neutral grade, eye level, rectangular crops on a hairline, in a dense 6-up grid with 'Nonprofits I support' captions naming real clients; the cabin-retreat candid as a full-width plate with a credit line; a credentials line (Google Ad Grants Certified, inaugural cohort · Google Partner · Inc. 5000, four years).
- 10. '07 Guides' (5/7). The ungated Ad Grants guide as a featured long read with reading time and last-reviewed date; the latest three posts with dates and bylines restored.
- 11. CTA band on the blue #0A23A2 (the second and last block of blue on the page). One headline in white Newsreader, one white-on-blue outlined 'Book a free call' button, one line of small print with the phone number, 'Am I eligible?' and Amber's email. The hero's fine print repeats here verbatim.
- 12. Footer as a colophon on newsprint. Four ruled columns, the real Beaverton, OR address, Google Partner and Ramp badges, the EmailOctopus field, 'Client reports' login, and a print stylesheet so case studies, the guarantee page and the account report survive board-forwarded PDFs with the ledger legible.
imagery: No illustration system and no stock. Photography is content, not palette: the no-chromatic rule governs the interface, not the pictures. Three registers. (1) NPM's own people, shot in natural light with a neutral, slightly cool grade (no warm push), eye level, rectangular crops on a hairline, captioned with name, role and 'Nonprofits I support'. In the first viewport only, the single portrait (Amber Snow in the signed note) is printed as a blue duotone plate, #0A23A2 on #EEF1FA with a fine halftone screen, so the hero holds to two inks; account-lead portraits on the monthly note use the same duotone. (2) Client work as documents: real Ad Grant dashboard screens and monthly reports reproduced at reading size, with a caption, a date, and a visible REDACTED tag on anything withheld; treated as figures in an article. (3) Beneficiary photography supplied by clients, dignity-first and consented, used sparingly as full-width plates with a credit line. Iconography is limited to arrows, the numbered-section system and the megaphone mark, redrawn as true vector in blue and ink; its signal arcs are the one proprietary device, drawn in white at low opacity inside the blue ledger header and as the progress rule on the eligibility checker. Data visualisation is the primary visual language: horizontal bar ledgers as inline SVG with computed geometry, utilisation meters drawn as thin rules, and the dashed blue Google floor at a computed x in every CTR chart. Chart palette: ink for NPM series, #0A23A2 for Google references and thresholds, #D9D9D6 for benchmarks, hatch for anything unsourced, labelled illustrative in the chart itself. Client marks are typeset (serif small caps, italic, tracked grotesk) with licensed monochrome logos allowed where recognition matters.
motion: Print does not move, so motion is limited to what a page does when you read it. Native scroll only; no smooth-scroll library. GSAP (free in Webflow) for three devices, all static-first so the page is complete without JavaScript: (1) ledger figures count up from zero in tabular figures on first view, 900ms, power2.out, then stay static; (2) SVG chart bars draw left to right on scroll-enter with the blue floor line and its label appearing last; (3) section rules extend from 0 to 100% width as they enter, 600ms, so the page feels ruled as you read. Headlines and body fade and translate 12px, staggered 40ms, never split-text or kinetic. Hover on links: the 1px underline thickens to 2px in blue; the primary button darkens to #071A7C, no lift, no shadow. The eligibility checker advances with a horizontal slide between questions while its progress rule fills; the honest not-eligible end card simply fades in. The monthly-note plate and the Hurtado endorsement do not animate at all; the human objects are always already there. prefers-reduced-motion: every device resolves to its final state instantly and transitions are disabled, which the mockups already implement. No parallax, no WebGL, no Lottie, no marquee; the client roll is static.
mobile: The 390px hero is a single column with the order fixed in CSS: ear strip (dateline left, 'Figures updated Sep 2026' right, 28px), compact masthead (mark + wordmark at 20px, a 40px 'Book a call' button, a 44px menu target) under the Oxford rule, then small-caps kicker, h1 at 44px/1.0 (three lines), a shortened deck at 16.5px (four lines), a full-width 48px blue 'Book a free call · 15 min' button, the 'Am I eligible? 4 questions · no email' link, and the fine-print line. In the mockup the button sits at about 420px from the top and the eligibility link at about 490px, well inside a 760px fold. Beneath the fold: the ledger condensed to a white card with the blue header and a 2x2 ruled grid of figures at 32px (780+, $48M+, 100%, 1 of 9) with a one-line footer stating the 5% floor and the published CTR range; the CTR chart itself moves to section 02 on phones. The single trust element is the client roll with its count ('780+ clients on record · 54 case studies') wrapping to two lines. The human row (Hurtado, Amber) follows the ledger on the next scroll. Key sections on phone: the policy table becomes a stacked list of ruled entries with the three headings as labels; the monthly note and statement stack 1/1 with the note first; case studies stack with the KPI trio as a 3-up strip; the client roll wraps; the team grid is 2-up. Labels floor at 11px, secondary gray holds AA on both grounds.
a11y: WCAG 2.2 AA is the target at every size, AAA for body. Measured on the actual grounds: ink #111 on #FAFAF8 17.5:1 and on white 18.3:1; secondary #56565A on #FAFAF8 7.0:1 and on white 7.4:1 (so 11px labels pass AA with margin); blue #0A23A2 on #FAFAF8 11.3:1 and on white 11.9:1; white on blue 11.9:1; ink on the #EEF1FA tint 16:1; chart tick gray #56565A on white 7.4:1; the hatched illustrative bar uses #8A8A8E strokes at 3.4:1 as a non-text graphic (3:1 required). Smallest text is 11px (ear strip and labels on phone); body 17px desktop, 16.5px phone. Focus: a 3px #0A23A2 outline with 3px offset on every link and button (:focus-visible), visible on newsprint, on white and around the blue button because of the offset gap. Targets: 48px primary buttons, 44px menu target, 40px compact nav button with 8px clearance. Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion (final states, transitions off). Text equivalents: the CTR chart is role=img with an aria-label that states every value and the floor; the portrait plate is role=img with a label; the logo slot is labelled as a placeholder; the megaphone mark, signal arcs, quote glyph and signature are aria-hidden decorative SVG. The ledger is an aside labelled 'Figures on the record', the hero is labelled by the h1, and the trust strip is a labelled region. Colour is never the only carrier of meaning: the floor line is dashed and labelled, the illustrative bar is hatched and labelled, links are underlined, and the active nav link is underlined as well as blue.

heroCopy.eyebrow: The Google Ad Grant · $10,000 a month in search ads for every eligible nonprofit
heroCopy.headline: Ten thousand dollars a month, properly spent.
heroCopy.sub: Most nonprofits never spend the full grant, and a 5% click-through rule can quietly switch it off. Nonprofit Megaphone manages the Ad Grant for 780+ organizations: $48M+ in donated media so far, a written acquisition guarantee, and a named account team that reports every month.

signatureMoments: The ear strip and masthead: a real dateline on the left, the certification line in the centre, 'Figures updated Sep 2026' and the client-reports login on the right, all above a Newsreader wordmark and an Oxford rule, so the first pixel of the page is a paper of record with today's date, not a publishing conceit.

The 'On the record' ledger: a white card whose header is the page's only block of brand blue (Google Partner badge, as-of date, the megaphone's signal arcs in white), four dated figures in tabular Newsreader, and an inline SVG CTR chart whose Google 5% floor is a dashed blue line at a computed x and whose only unsourced bar is hatched and labelled illustrative in the chart itself.

One blue, used like a newspaper's spot colour: the headline's italic 'properly spent.', the CTA, the eligibility underline, the floor line, Michelle Hurtado's title, Amber Snow's signature and her duotone portrait are all the same #0A23A2, so the eye learns in one view that blue means 'the thing that matters here'.

The three-column foot of the hero: Google's first Head of Ad Grants on one side of a hairline, Amber Snow's signed 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy.' on the other, the ledger beside both, so endorsement, accountability and evidence sit on one ruled line.

The typographic client roll between column rules, capped at six with one licensed monochrome logo slot, headed '780+ clients on record · 54 published case studies · updated monthly', so the trust strip reads as a subscriber list rather than a badge wall.
dependencies: Publish a price range for Ad Grant management (flat monthly fee, no percent of spend) and confirm the 100% acquisition guarantee wording as a clause; section 04 and the hero fine print depend on it.
Name account leads publicly and commit operations to a real one-sentence monthly note per rotating client, with a consent process; section 02 depends on it.
Consent from one client for a real, redacted monthly report to render as the statement and the 'See a real account report' PDF.
A CMS 'figures last updated' field and a 'last reviewed' date that drive the ear strip; the masthead line must never be hand-edited.
A licensed benchmark (M+R or equivalent) for the unmanaged-median bar, or agree to remove it; the hatched illustrative bar is a placeholder.

Verify the three case-study CTR figures in the hero chart (Scouting America 25.2%, ACC of New York 14.0%, Spotting Cancer 7.5%) and the 'published case studies run 7.5% to 25.2%' line on the phone against the live case-study pages before the pitch; ACC of New York and Spotting Cancer are also outside the approved client-wordmark list. If any figure cannot be sourced, swap that row for a sourced one or hatch it and label it illustrative like the median bar.
Confirm the mark's actual blue against #0A23A2 and redraw the megaphone as true vector; agree the wordmark reset to Newsreader.
Check Google Partner badge brand rules for placement on a #0A23A2 block; if a reversed badge is not permitted, the badge moves to the white row beneath the header.
A photography session for the 60-person team under a neutral grade, plus the CEO and account-lead portraits that become the duotone plates.
Permission to use licensed monochrome logos for the marks that need recognition (Scouting America, UNCF); the typographic roll covers the rest.
A small GSAP sprint (count-up, bar draw, rule extend) and a locked Webflow class set with a style-guide page so editors cannot add shadows or radii.
risks: Serif-on-white editorial is a broad lane; ownability rests on the ledger, the dated masthead and the one-blue discipline. If leadership will not publish pricing, real account figures or named leads, the concept degrades to a well-set template.

One chromatic colour is a strict diet. A Webflow editor adding a green success state or a yellow star rating breaks the system faster than any content change; the style guide and locked classes are load-bearing.

Photography that is only duotone would read as archival; the direction keeps natural colour for the team page and case studies and restricts duotone to the hero and monthly-note plates. If the client wants warm-graded people photography everywhere, this direction is the wrong fit and Signed Sentence is the better home.

The direction is only as strong as the evidence it prints: it needs real monthly report screens, a licensed benchmark to replace the hatched bar, dated bylines and a CMS last-updated field driving the ear strip. The mockup marks every placeholder as such; the build must keep that honesty.

Cool newsprint plus black ink can read cold next to the company's warm voice ('No Drama Llama', the $25 handshake). The human row in the hero and the signed monthly note carry the warmth; cutting either in production would leave the page austere.

Editorial layouts are text-heavy; the hero is the most type-dense of the set. The phone contract (44px h1, CTA and eligibility link before the ledger, 32px figures, chart deferred to section 02) is written into the mobile mockup and must be prototyped in Webflow, not assumed.

Small-caps section labels rely on Newsreader's OpenType small caps; if a browser synthesises them the labels get slightly heavier. Acceptable, but the type scale should be checked on Windows once the fonts are self-hosted.
references: The New York Times and The Guardian's masthead, ear-strip and column-rule structure for the newspaper grammar without the costume
Stripe Press (press.stripe.com) for serif authority and ruled layouts
Bloomberg.com and Businessweek data typography and ledger tables
The Economist's single-colour discipline: one red used as a spot colour on otherwise monochrome pages, translated here to one blue
The Pudding for charts as the argument rather than decoration
Mercury.com Journal for tabular numerals and serif pull quotes in a finance context
McKinsey Insights for numbered sections and calm institutional pacing
Duotone press plates (Pentagram's work for The Public Theater and Yale's identity) for the one-ink portrait treatment
